title: Was bubble wrap invented as wallpaper? Yes, really

sources.name: Sealed Air — The origins of Bubble Wrap

practice: Fancy another unexpected fact? Try a round of General Knowledge.

sections.html:
Yes. Bubble wrap began in 1957 as an attempt to make textured wallpaper. Engineers Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes joined two plastic sheets with pockets of air trapped between them in Hawthorne, New Jersey.

Sealed Air tells the story of the original wall covering. Picture the sheet from your last parcel spread across a living-room wall: the decorating plan was rather different from the result we know.
sections.title: Wallpaper before wrapping paper

sections.html:
The wallpaper idea did not take off, but the air pockets offered another use: cushioning objects during shipping.

1957 was the original experiment; 1960 was the founding of Sealed Air. Fielding and Chavannes started the company with Bubble Wrap as its signature product, according to its published history.
sections.title: Why do both 1957 and 1960 appear?

sections.html:
The material’s useful feature was there all along. Air pockets gave the plastic its unusual texture; they also helped it protect objects. What changed was where people used it.

It is not the only everyday object with an unexpected beginning. Post-it notes also found a use for an initially awkward result. Next time you open a parcel, spare a thought for the living-room wall that never happened.
sections.title: A second job for a strange idea

description: Bubble wrap began as textured wallpaper in 1957, before finding a home inside parcels. Meet the two inventors and the idea that changed direction.
